constructs.label: Age group
constructs.definition: Age in four adult bands: 18-29, 30-44, 45-64, 65+.

constructs.label: Candidate trait: cares
constructs.definition: How well 'really cares about people like you' describes the major-party presidential candidate named in item_text.

constructs.label: Candidate trait: honest
constructs.definition: How well 'honest' describes the major-party presidential candidate named in item_text.

constructs.label: Candidate trait: knowledgeable
constructs.definition: How well 'knowledgeable' describes the major-party presidential candidate named in item_text.

constructs.label: Candidate trait: strong leadership
constructs.definition: How well 'provides strong leadership' describes the major-party presidential candidate named in item_text.

constructs.label: Citizenship
constructs.definition: Citizen by birth (born in the U.S., Puerto Rico or the U.S. Island Areas, or abroad to an American parent); Naturalized citizen; Not a citizen.

constructs.label: Favorability of closed primaries
constructs.definition: Favorable or unfavorable view of primaries closed to all but registered party members.

constructs.label: Confidence in Congress
constructs.definition: Confidence in the people running Congress (the national legislature).

constructs.label: Confidence in the executive branch
constructs.definition: Confidence in the people running the executive branch of the federal government.

constructs.label: Confidence in the press
constructs.definition: Confidence in the people running the press.

constructs.label: Citizen voting-age population
constructs.definition: U.S. citizens aged 18 and over. pct rows give the share of the 18+ population, overall or within a group, who are citizens.

constructs.label: Education
constructs.definition: Highest level completed, four groups: HS or less (no schooling through a high school diploma or GED); Some college (some college without a degree, or an associate's degree); BA (bachelor's degree); Grad (master's, professional or doctorate degree).

constructs.label: External political efficacy
constructs.definition: Belief that officials care what people like the respondent think and that people like them have a say.

constructs.label: Internal political efficacy
constructs.definition: Belief that politics and government are not too complicated for the respondent to understand.

constructs.label: Egalitarianism
constructs.definition: Agreement with statements about equal opportunity and equal treatment; item_text gives the statement and its direction.

constructs.label: Elections are fair
constructs.definition: Agreement that elections are fair and accurately conducted, at the level named in item_text.

constructs.label: How people get ahead
constructs.definition: Whether hard work or luck and help from others matters most for getting ahead.

constructs.label: Government should reduce income differences
constructs.definition: Support for government action to reduce income differences between rich and poor.

constructs.label: Ideology, 5-point
constructs.definition: Self-description from very liberal to very conservative on five points.

constructs.label: Ideology, 7-point
constructs.definition: Self-placement on a seven-point scale from extremely liberal to extremely conservative.

constructs.label: Income differences too large
constructs.definition: Agreement that differences in income in America are too large.

constructs.label: Lift: comprehension
constructs.definition: Effect of a tested cut on comprehension, arm minus placebo, in percentage points.

constructs.label: Lift: candidate favorability
constructs.definition: Effect of one ad on the favorability index for its campaign's candidate, ad arm minus placebo, in points on a 0-100 scale.

constructs.label: Lift: support
constructs.definition: Effect of a tested cut on support, arm minus placebo, in percentage points.

constructs.label: Lift: vote choice
constructs.definition: Effect of one ad on the vote-choice index for its campaign's candidate, ad arm minus placebo, in points on a 0-100 scale.

constructs.label: Lift: vote choice, dichotomized
constructs.definition: Effect of one ad on the share leaning to its campaign's candidate (vote-choice index above its midpoint, exactly at it counting half), in percentage points.

constructs.label: National pride
constructs.definition: How proud the respondent is of being American.

constructs.label: National pride by domain
constructs.definition: How proud the respondent is of America in the domain named in item_text.

constructs.label: Nationalism
constructs.definition: Agreement that America is better than other countries or that one would rather be its citizen than any other's.

constructs.label: Support for open primaries
constructs.definition: Support for primaries open to all voters, as asked in a poll or decided by a ballot measure; item_text gives each wording.

constructs.label: Parties care about opinions
constructs.definition: Whether parties are interested in people's opinions and not only their votes.

constructs.label: Party identification, 7-point
constructs.definition: Party identification from strong Democrat to strong Republican, with independents who lean to a party placed beside it.

constructs.label: People try to be fair
constructs.definition: Whether most people would try to be fair or take advantage of you given the chance.

constructs.label: People try to be helpful
constructs.definition: Whether people mostly try to be helpful or mostly look out for themselves.

constructs.label: Which of the following was the main reason (you/name) (were/was) not registered to vote?
constructs.definition: Which of the following was the main reason (you/name) (were/was) not registered to vote?

constructs.label: Which of the following was the main reason (you/name) (were/was) not registered to vote? (2020)
constructs.definition: Which of the following was the main reason (you/name) (were/was) not registered to vote?

constructs.label: What was the main reason (you/name) did not vote?
constructs.definition: What was the main reason (you/name) did not vote?

constructs.label: What was the main reason (you/name) did not vote? (2020)
constructs.definition: What was the main reason (you/name) did not vote?

constructs.label: Did (you/he/she) vote in person or did (you/he/she) vote by mail?
constructs.definition: Did (you/he/she) vote in person or did (you/he/she) vote by mail?

constructs.label: Was that on election day or before election day?
constructs.definition: Was that on election day or before election day?

constructs.label: There are various places and ways people can register to vote. The last time (you/name) registered, how did (you/name) register to vote?
constructs.definition: There are various places and ways people can register to vote. The last time (you/name) registered, how did (you/name) register to vote?

constructs.label: There are various places and ways people can register to vote. The last time (you/name) registered, how did (you/name) register to vote? (2008)
constructs.definition: There are various places and ways people can register to vote. The last time (you/name) registered, how did (you/name) register to vote?

constructs.label: How long (have you/has name) lived at this address? (2008-2012)
constructs.definition: How long (have you/has name) lived at this address?

constructs.label: Presidential job approval
constructs.definition: Approval of the way the sitting president is handling the job.

constructs.label: Party primary voted in, validated
constructs.definition: Among adults with a voter-file record of voting in the primary named in item_text, whose primary they voted in.

constructs.label: Primary turnout, validated
constructs.definition: Share of adults with a voter-file record of voting in the primary named in item_text; respondents with no record count as non-voters.

constructs.label: How long (have you/has name) lived at this address?
constructs.definition: How long (have you/has name) lived at this address?

constructs.label: Race and ethnicity
constructs.definition: Five exclusive groups: Hispanic or Latino (any race); then, among non-Hispanic people, White alone; Black alone; Asian or Pacific Islander (Asian alone, or Native Hawaiian and Other Pacific Islander alone); Other or multiracial (American Indian and Alaska Native alone, some other race alone, two or more races).

constructs.label: Voter registration
constructs.definition: Registered to vote for the given election.

constructs.label: Registration by party
constructs.definition: Registered voters by party enrollment, unenrolled status, or political designation, as the Secretary of the Commonwealth counts them.

constructs.label: Religious service attendance
constructs.definition: How often the respondent attends religious services.

constructs.label: Sex
constructs.definition: Sex as reported: Male or Female.

constructs.label: Generalized social trust
constructs.definition: Whether most people can be trusted or one needs to be careful in dealing with people.

constructs.label: Feeling thermometer: Democratic Party
constructs.definition: Warmth toward the Democratic Party on a 0-100 thermometer.

constructs.label: Feeling thermometer: Republican Party
constructs.definition: Warmth toward the Republican Party on a 0-100 thermometer.

constructs.label: Favorability of top-four primaries
constructs.definition: Favor or oppose a top-four primary, where all candidates share one ballot and the four leading vote-getters advance, as in Alaska.

constructs.label: Favorability of top-two primaries
constructs.definition: Favorable or unfavorable view of a top-two primary, where all candidates share one ballot and the two leading vote-getters advance.

constructs.label: Trust in the federal government
constructs.definition: How much the federal government in Washington can be trusted to do what is right or to handle the nation's problems.

constructs.label: Turnout
constructs.definition: Voted in the given election.
